A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LoRA.rar. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison across relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation comparisons, MARS2 evaluations, a 25-participant human study, resource measurements and hypernetwork ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds KOALA-700M experiments, metric-to-human correlations, and evaluations on new concepts and category-disjoint splits.

M1.justification: The column-wise hypernetwork, query/output merging with key/value averaging, loss in Equation 3 and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. v2 expands the explanation of repurposing ZipLoRA's loss and evaluates another backbone without documenting a changed merging procedure.

E1.justification: Section A2.5 adds evaluation on toaster, television and sofa subjects and a cyberpunk style. The original DreamBooth and StyleDrop/ZipLoRA coverage and joint subject-style generation task remain. The new backbone and repartitioning experiments primarily change settings rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain Joint Training, Direct Merge, DARE, TIES, DARE-TIES and ZipLoRA. The added backbone and generalization experiments reuse ZipLoRA; no new comparison method is introduced. DreamCache is cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation design with KOALA-700M and two retrained, category-disjoint configurations: objects/3D renderings to stuffed animals/cartoons, and animals/watercolors to objects/other styles (Section A2.6). These are additional protocols; the original SDXL settings and hyperparameters are retained, with implementation details moved to Section A1.3.

E4.justification: v2 adds metric-to-human alignment analysis, lightweight-backbone testing, new-concept generalization and two controlled category-shift studies. These examine metric validity and generalization beyond v1's analyses. The original component ablations, per-subject/style heatmaps, failure example and recontextualization studies remain.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 newly estimates correlations between human scores and CLIP-I, DINO and MARS2 for Direct Merge. This adds statistical association analysis, although the correlation type and sampling details are unspecified. Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Substantial new findings include KOALA average/best MARS2 scores of 0.56/0.92 for LoRA.rar versus 0.51/0.84 for ZipLoRA, new-concept scores of 0.8 versus 0.6, and human correlations of 0.08, -0.01 and 0.76 for CLIP-I, DINO and MARS2. New qualitative generalization results accompany these. Original SDXL scores, human-preference percentages, resource measurements and ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, column-independence assumption, merging equations and training objective are retained. v2 adds explanatory and empirical arguments, but no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 promotes the curated LoRA-weight dataset to an explicit contribution and describes weights as a valuable data modality. The central claims about zero-shot merging, MARS2, image quality and over-4000-fold merging speedup remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 strengthens the merging-coefficient interpretation from possible integration limitations to an explicit ZipLoRA overfitting explanation, and explains training-data sufficiency through column-wise examples. Section A3.1 removes the hypothesis that the can fails because it differs from training subjects and the suggested remedy of broader LoRA training, while retaining text-rendering and MLLM-detail limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link, brief acquisition information for the new subjects, and states that the new split experiments reuse existing hyperparameters. Original architecture, optimization settings and evaluation prompts are retained; moving implementation details into Section A1.3 is not a new disclosure.

R1.justification: v2 adds DreamCache and KOALA citations. The principal positioning relative to ZipLoRA and earlier hypernetwork approaches remains. Several other references receive publication or title updates corresponding to existing cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and explanation revisions, reorganizes Section 5.1, and moves standard-metric discussion and implementation details into the appendix. The main section structure and most existing prose remain, alongside new appendix subsections.

P2.justification: v2 adds the KOALA results table and three appendix figures covering backbone and generalization experiments. It also replaces Figure 1's examples, revises overview/evaluation diagrams and coefficient-plot styling, and relocates the standard-metric table and coefficient analysis. These constitute a substantial visual expansion and rearrangement; existing qualitative grids and ablation displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The added backbone and category-shift tests strengthen generalization evidence, while the correlation analysis provides additional support for MARS2. The gains are limited by underspecified correlation methodology and stronger causal interpretations without corresponding mechanism tests. Section 5.1 also incorrectly calls Direct Merge highest on DINO: Table A2 reports 0.747 versus Joint Training's 0.764. Overall, the added validation provides a modest net improvement.
